scope: Read-only local UI latency investigation. No production edits, router operations, app restart or visual changes.
environment: Windows, Python 3.10, PySide6, Qt offscreen; synthetic AP list and temporary settings file. Profiling overhead applies to profile measurements.

findings.result: Accept/reject close callback is below 1 ms here; full dialog construction/show/cancel is slower. Main measured hotspot: common theme construction, QSS scaling and application.

Page save callbacks synchronously normalize paths and write configuration in the UI thread. Cost increases with dictionary path count. Temporary single-file measurement does not characterize every deployed storage configuration.

Settings dialog finished signal unconditionally emits settingsChanged; closing an unchanged editor still enters settings collection/normalization/save. Split persistence may skip unchanged writes, but normalization remains synchronous.
Stop callback requests cancellation only; no synchronous worker join or remote cleanup wait found in that direct path. State signals can still trigger UI updates.
Unchanged AP lists return early and measured sub-ms; initial list rebuild scales with count and can briefly stall UI.

limits: Not a reproduction of a specific live user click or multi-second freeze.
No full desktop CPU/GPU or event-dispatch tracing; offscreen timings differ from visible rendering.
suggested_scope: Optimize shared dialog theme reuse and configuration normalization/persistence boundaries first; keep appearance and router behavior unchanged.
